title: Rav Kahana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Seder HaDorot already discussed at length how many Rav Kahanas there were. After much examination Hyman considers it clear that there were no fewer than five Amoraim named Rav Kahana: (1) the student-colleague of Rav and colleague of Rav Assi; (2) Rav’s student; (3) Rav Kahana, Rav Yehudah’s student. All three went up to the Land of Israel: the first went up in his old age and remained there; the second went up in his youth, in Rabbi Yochanan’s time, and afterward went down to Babylonia; the third went to the Land of Israel and lived there many years. (4) Rava’s great student, from whom Rav Ashi received, and who was head in Pum Nahara. (5) Rav Ashi’s colleague.

notes.text: The five numbered items are editorial organization of Hyman’s unnumbered list. His “no fewer than five” distinction is retained as his argued conclusion, not a count of distinct people established by this review.

The consulted Seder HaDorot discussion explicitly contrasts a two-person scheme attributed to Tosafot with a three-person scheme attributed to Yuchasin and organizes the relationships together. This confirms the existence of the earlier discussion, not Hyman’s different “no fewer than five” conclusion, which remains his argued distinction.
